 Kane Williamson predicts next crop of 'Fab Four' batters
 New Zealand great Kane Williamson has reflected on his time alongside Virat Kohli, Steve Smith and Joe Root in the 'Fab Four' for Test batters and anointed the next group of stars that he thinks might fill the mantle.
 19 November, 2026 Kane Williamson’s autobiography ‘The Bare Margins’ is now available. 
 Kane Williamson shocked the cricketing world earlier this year when he called time on his illustrious 16-year international career, with the Black Caps legend departing the game with a remarkable resume that included a New Zealand record of 33 Test centuries, a total of 9,515 Test runs while holding the premier position as the No.1 batter on the ICC Men's Test Batting Rankings for a lengthy period.
 Among the long list of accolades across all formats, Williamson was also deservedly included as a member of the 'Fab Four' in recent times alongside a group of his contemporaries - Virat Kohli, Steve Smith and Joe Root - that have dominated Test cricket with the bat since the turn of the century.
 Kane Williamson on stepping away, the call with Virat Kohli, the Fab Four and what comes next | The ICC Review
 Kane Williamson joins Nasser Hussain in the latest The ICC Review to chat retirement and how a call with Virat Kohli made the decision clear. Williamson also looks back on the note he wrote to himself as a 22-year-old in Colombo about what success should mean, the 2019 Cricket World Cup final and the 2021 World Test Championship win.
 Williamson spoke with host Nasser Hussain on the most recent episode of The ICC Review about his standing within the 'Fab Four' and the former New Zealand skipper admitted he never felt any additional pressure being recognised among his fellow peers in an exclusive group of Test greats.
 "I never felt a burden with it," Williamson said.
 "I admired those other three that you mentioned of the 'Fab Four' and I know them all well having played with Rooty at Yorkshire and obviously against them for a long time.
 "I really did admire them and love the way they go about it, and they're all very, very different."
 While Williamson admitted it was special to reach individual milestones and be mentioned among the other members of the 'Fab Four' throughout his career, he said his only focus when representing New Zealand was based upon upholding team values and helping the Black Caps win games of cricket.
 Kane Williamson on the Kohli call that made retirement clear | The ICC Review
 "For me it was just it was always about what you can do for the team and how you keep doing more, and I did love the team focus because it's also a great way to keep extending your game and that it's never enough," Williamson noted.
 "That was where my focus was, and it was about just trying to make valuable contributions for the team. Yeah, rather than it's very difficult to just compare and measure, and it's not a very fun thing to do, but it's also you just you're constantly playing in different conditions, you know, at different times, and so, yeah, it just kind of lands where it does.
 "I never thought a lot about it when I played, but looking back since retiring, it's quite sort of unique in some ways. There are four of us that sort of hung around for a while and scored a few runs."
 Australia's 'amazing talent' Cameron Green | WTC23 Final
 Australia all-rounder Cameron Green is out to make his mark in the ICC World Test Championship Final 2023 against India
 With Williamson and Kohli having already called time on their Test careers and Smith and Root closer to the finish than the start of theirs, there remains plenty of intrigue over the next crop of Test batters and who will step up over time and create their own 'Fab Four'.
 Hussain asked Williamson for his thoughts on this subject and he nominated five players that he thought might be able to elevate their game and join a new exclusive group of Test stars.
 "I have answered this question before actually, so I'd better say the same otherwise (it is) a bit of a fraud," Williamson joked.
 "But I had Harry Brook, I had Shubman Gill , I had Cameron Green and I actually had Yashasvi Jaiswal too.
 "And there was another one, but that was Rachin Ravindra. But I think maybe a challenge he might have is the volume of cricket and maybe Test cricket, because I don't know where that will land, but he would be in there for me too."
